name: Streetscape Visual Complexity in Tianjin (Low / Medium / High)
description:
Method replication: same task, scale and design as the paper; the images are not the paper's stimuli (117 Baidu street views re-fetched in the Wudadao and Xiaobailou districts of Heping District, Tianjin, 2015 or later; one of four directions per point, 90° field of view).

Original study: Zhao & Suo (2024), Land 13(11), 1953. Baidu street views were taken every 40 m in four directions (0°, 90°, 180°, 270°) across Wudadao and Xiaobailou. 15 students and professors in landscape architecture first agreed the scoring criteria on a subset, then each independently rated the visual complexity of 560 random images as low (1), medium (2) or high (3). Rounded mean scores trained an SVM model on image features (compression ratio, grey-level contrast, hierarchical complexity, fractal dimension, colour complexity, symmetry) to map complexity across the districts.

Differences from the original study: (1) 117 new images instead of 560; each participant rates all of them in random order. (2) The joint calibration session among the experts is replaced by a one-line description of complexity on the first page. (3) Anyone can take part; a background question records whether the participant is a student, teacher or practitioner in landscape architecture or planning.
